query: Derive per-layer time and memory complexity formulas for HyperConv (sparse SpMM), SSM variants (full, low-rank+diag, Cayley, negative-definite), and cross-attention; what intermediate activations dominate memory?

response.query: Derive per-layer time and memory complexity formulas for HyperConv (sparse SpMM), SSM variants (full, low-rank+diag, Cayley, negative-definite), and cross-attention; what intermediate activations dominate memory?
response.answer: Per-layer time complexity for HyperConv is O(n^2), and memory complexity is O(n). For SSM variants, full has O(n^2), low-rank+diag O(n log n), Cayley O(n^2), and negative-definite O(n^3). Cross-attention has O(n^2) time and O(n) memory.

results.title: Sparse Attention Variants Overview
results.content: * Sparse attention variants are techniques that reduce computational and memory demands by structuring or learning sparsity in attention mechanisms. Sparse attention variants comprise a diverse collection of mechanisms for reducing the computational and memory complexity of attention in deep neural models by restricting, structuring, or learning sparsity patterns in the attention matrix or computation graph. These approaches encompass fixed and learned sparsification, regularization-driven sparsity, dynamic data- or content-based masking, continuous-domain sparse projections, and highly optimized hardware-aware sparse formats. Examples include SPARSEK Attention (Lou et al., 2024), Mixture of Sparse Attention (MoSA) (Piękos et al., 1 May 2025), dynamic mask attention (Shi et al., 4 Aug 2025), and learnable edge selection in Sparse Graph Attention Networks (SGAT) (Ye et al., 2019). * **Efficient Hardware-Aware Sparse Implementations:** GPU code generation, layout-optimized sparse formats, and query grouping to maximize hardware utilization as in SPLAT (Gupta et al., 2024) and Flash Sparse Attention (FSA) (Yan et al., 25 Aug 2025).

results.title: [PDF] Backprop with Approximate Activations for Memory-efficient Network ...
results.content: In particular, training such networks requires a signiﬁcant amount of on-device GPU memory—much more so than during inference—in order to store activations of all intermediate layers of the network that are needed for gradient computation during back-propagation. In this work, we propose a new backprop algorithm based on the following key observations: the forward pass through a network can be computed exactly without storing intermediate activations, and approximating activations has minimal effect on gradients “ﬂowing back” to the input of a layer in the backward pass. For the forward pass during training, our method uses a layer’s exact activations to compute those for a subsequent layer. 3.4 Network Architectures and Memory Usage Our full training algorithm applies our approximation strategy to every layer (deﬁned by grouping linear transforms with preceding non-linear activations) during the forward and backward pass.

results.title: [PDF] Scatterbrain: Unifying Sparse and Low-rank Attention Approximation
results.content: Scatterbrain: Unifying Sparse and Low-rank Attention Approximation Beidi Chen⇤†, Tri Dao⇤†, Eric Winsor †, Zhao Song §, Atri Rudra ‡, Christopher Ré † † Department of Computer Science, Stanford University § Adobe Research ‡ Department of Computer Science and Engineering, University at Buffalo, SUNY {beidic,trid,winsor,chrismre}@stanford.edu, zsong@adobe.com, atri@buffalo.edu Abstract Recent advances in efﬁcient Transformers have exploited either the sparsity or low-rank properties of attention matrices to reduce the computational and memory bottlenecks of modeling long sequences. Fig. 3 shows a qualitative comparison between different methods of approximating the attention matrix: Robust PCA is accurate but slow, sparse (e.g., Reformer), and low-rank (e.g., Performer) attention are fast and memory-efﬁcient but may not be very accurate, while Scatterbrain is more accurate than its sparse and low-rank counterparts while remaining just as efﬁcient.

results.title: Turbocharging Transformers: Reducing Memory Footprint with Cross-Layer Attention | by QvickRead | GoPenAI
